requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: Verified no pre-existing appworker user, then created with useradd -m; id confirmed uid=1000(appworker). Account persisted and resolved correctly after the subsequent reboot.

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8,192 open files and 256 processes
requirements.summary: Wrote /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf with soft/hard nofile 8192 and soft/hard nproc 256, confirmed pam_limits.so active in system-auth, and directly verified via a real su - appworker login session showing ulimit -n=8192 and ulimit -u=256. Re-verified identically after the node restart.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — creating the appworker account and constraining its login sessions to 8,192 open files / 256 processes — are directly satisfied with evidence from a real su - login session, not just configuration inspection. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol is also fully and coherently demonstrated: a pre-restart healthy baseline (boot_id 7223d5b7..., systemctl is-system-running=running), an acknowledged systemctl reboot, observed connection loss during the disruption, a different post-restart boot_id (f377f98c...), and full recovery of the account, its resource limits, and overall system health afterward. Lifecycle snapshots corroborate the boot-identity change and show no unwanted residue beyond an expected reboot log artifact.
limitations: The preparation phase was disabled (before_prepare and after_prepare are identical aliases), so no prepare-vs-executor state separation was needed here.
Node health during the restart window is inferred from connection failures rather than an explicit degraded-state capture, though this is consistent with a genuine reboot.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command sequence is tight and purposeful: OS/account check, user creation, limits file write, PAM verification via a real login session, then the mandatory restart-evidence protocol (baseline boot_id/health capture, background systemctl reboot, connection-drop polling, post-restart boot_id and full re-verification of account/limits/system health). No unnecessary or destructive mutations were found; every state-changing command maps directly to satisfying the task or the restart protocol. The only residue is /tmp/reboot.log, an inherent artifact of backgrounding systemctl reboot via nohup redirection — low-risk, expected, and not indicative of abandoned or unsafe state. Failed-services and package-health checks show no damage before or after.
